name: Kodak Professional T-MAX 400 (400TMY)
notes: Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds, as printed; the plots say 'Exposure: Daylight'. No Log H Ref is printed.

curves/v: T-MAX RS Developer and Replenisher, large tank, 24 C (75 F), 5 minutes, the sheet's recommended starting time for that developer (page 3, large-tank rolls), which the sheet's contrast-index chart puts at about 0.56 (the chart's lines start at 0.42). Same plot: v-tmaxrs-7, v-tmaxrs-9.

Further plots, one per panel of page 8: 'curves-d76' = D-76, small tank, 20 C (68 F), 6/8/11 min (v-d76-6, -8, -11; recommended 7 1/2 min, so v-d76-8 is the nearest, contrast index about 0.6); 'curves-tmax' = T-MAX Developer, small tank, 24 C (75 F), 5/7/9 min (v-tmax-5, -7, -9; recommended 5 1/2 min).

Spectral sensitivity (page 7): Developer D-76, 20 C (68 F), diffuse visual, no exposure time printed; sensitivity/v is the dotted curve 'D=1.0 greater than D-min', v-d03 the solid curve 'D=0.3 greater than D-min'. Log sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) as printed. Both curves start near 360-400 nm and end near 650 nm.

Grain: diffuse rms granularity 10, read at net diffuse density 1.00 with a 48 micrometre aperture, 12x, development in D-76 at 68 F (IMAGE STRUCTURE section). Resolving power 50 lines/mm (TOC 1.6:1) and 200 lines/mm (TOC 1000:1).
Push: the sheet says EI 800 (one stop under) with normal development in most developers, EI 1600 with longer development and EI 3200 with a longer development again; no curves are plotted for them.
